title: Root branching repair: does the genome span two architectures?
question: Do these read as two different root architectures, or as more of the same thing? (Left is a low draw, right a high draw, same plant genome otherwise.)
context_md:
Genotype **slot 1 (root branch chance)** shipped in the genome re-map wired
correctly and produced a **bit-identical stand at every draw** — 352 root
cells at −1, 0 and +1 alike. Its consumer sat behind a gate that demanded a
*second* step's carbon in the same tick the first was paid: 351 root growth
steps in 12,000 frames, **2** could afford it, the 0.04 roll fired **0**
times.

The owner's call was that the allowance economy is intended and the
double-affordance gate is the accident. This is the primed-site repair from
PLAN.md's M16 note: a root tip **marks** a site every N steps for free, and
the site buys its lateral later, funded by the plant, when it can be paid
for. Slot 1 divides N, so a strong draw primes more densely.

Both images are the same scene, same seed, same frame (noon), 8 trees /
30,000 frames — **only the slot-1 draw differs**.

| | draw −1 | draw +1 |
|---|---|---|
| root cells, median | 251 | **776** |
| root cells with 3+ root neighbours | 57% | **78%** |
| lateral spread | 50 | 74 |
| whole-plant cells | 26,620 | **32,819** |

The question is whether these read as **two different root architectures**
or as more-of-the-same. A one-cell-wide run scores ~0 on the neighbour
metric whichever way it points, so that number is the architecture
discriminator — but it cannot tell you whether the difference is legible.
